categories.name: Email-Based Adversary Tradecraft
categories.description: How attackers abuse Exchange Online for persistence, access, and evasion.

ttps.name: Mailbox Email Forwarding
ttps.description: Attackers configure Victor Alvarez's mailbox to forward communications to archive@threat-actor.diaries.cn, maintaining persistent collection without continued authentication or malware.
ttps.enhancement: Retained and grounded in ATT&CK's exact Email Forwarding Rule sub-technique; the existing app-attribution pivots already exceed the source slide's single-table example.

references.title: Mail flow rules in Exchange Online

pivotSteps.purpose: Find an external forwarding change and collect the affected user and source IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
OfficeActivity
| where Operation == "Set-Mailbox"
| where tostring(Parameters) has "ForwardingSmtpAddress"
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Parameters

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UserId and ClientIP to identify the OAuth application that made the change.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "MailboxForwardingConfigured"
| where AccountId == "<UserId>" and IPAddress == "<ClientIP>"
| project Timestamp, OAuthAppId, ObjectName, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on OAuthAppId and IPAddress to the application sign-in that contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where AppId == "<OAuthAppId>" and IPAddress == "<IPAddress>"
| project TimeGenerated, ServicePrincipalName, UserAgent

ttps.name: Malicious Inbox Rules
ttps.description: Attackers create or modify inbox rules to hide security notifications, intercept messages, or redirect mail while avoiding user awareness.
ttps.enhancement: Expanded the source slide's broad rule hunt into a correlation chain that distinguishes mailbox manipulation from the interactive and background sessions that sustain it.

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a rule that suppresses security mail and collect the mailbox identity and source IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
OfficeActivity
| where Operation == "New-InboxRule"
| where tostring(Parameters) has_any ("DeleteMessage", "MoveToFolder")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Parameters

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UserId and ClientIP to recover the authentication session ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where UserPrincipalName == "<UserId>" and IPAddress == "<ClientIP>"
| where AppDisplayName == "Office 365 Exchange Online"
| where isnotempty(SessionId)
| project TimeGenerated, SessionId, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the automated continuation that contains the flag while each request retains a distinct CorrelationId.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where isnotempty(SessionId) and SessionId == "<SessionId>"
| project TimeGenerated, AppDisplayName, IncomingTokenType, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.name: Delegated Mailbox Permissions
ttps.description: Attackers grant an adversary-controlled identity FullAccess, SendAs, or SendOnBehalf rights so it can operate on a victim mailbox without authenticating as the mailbox owner.
ttps.enhancement: Mapped to the exact ATT&CK sub-technique for added email delegation and expanded from a single audit event into a delegate-to-session investigation path.

mitreAttack.name: Account Manipulation: Additional Email Delegate Permissions

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a mailbox permission grant and extract the delegate identity and source IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
OfficeActivity
| where Operation == "Add-MailboxPermission"
| where tostring(Parameters) has_any ("FullAccess", "SendAs", "SendOnBehalf")
| extend DelegateUpn=extract(@"User=([^;]+)", 1, tostring(Parameters))
| project TimeGenerated, Mailbox=OfficeObjectId, DelegateUpn, IPAddress=ClientIP

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the delegate and source IP to recover the Defender for Cloud Apps session ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "MailboxPermissionGranted"
| where AccountId == "<DelegateUpn>" and IPAddress == "<IPAddress>"
| extend SessionId=tostring(SessionData.SessionId)
| project Timestamp, AccountId, ObjectName, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the delegate's background Exchange access that contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, AuthenticationDetails

categories.name: Identity-Based Adversary Tradecraft
categories.description: How attackers abuse identity, authentication, and authorization to gain access and persist in cloud environments.

ttps.name: Suspicious Sign-In Patterns
ttps.description: Attackers use valid cloud credentials from unfamiliar infrastructure or unmanaged devices; the suspicious pattern is an analytic signal whose underlying ATT&CK behavior is valid cloud-account use.
ttps.enhancement: Corrected the source framing: Suspicious Sign-In Patterns is not a standalone ATT&CK technique. The challenge now maps the observed anomaly to T1078.004 and requires corroboration in Defender XDR sign-in telemetry.

references.title: Microsoft Entra sign-in log activity details

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a successful risky sign-in from an unmanaged device and collect its correlation ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0" and IsRisky and IsInteractive
| where tobool(parse_json(DeviceDetail).isManaged) == false
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, CorrelationId, DeviceDetail

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on CorrelationId to the Defender XDR view and inspect the authentication evidence containing the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
EntraIdSignInEvents
| where CorrelationId == "<CorrelationId>"
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, DeviceName, RiskLevelAggregated, AuthenticationProcessingDetails

ttps.validationKql:
let Seed = SigninLogs | where ResultType == "0" and IsRisky and IsInteractive and tobool(parse_json(DeviceDetail).isManaged) == false | project CorrelationId;
EntraIdSignInEvents | project CorrelationId, Flag=AuthenticationProcessingDetails | join kind=inner Seed on CorrelationId | project Flag

ttps.name: Token Abuse
ttps.description: Attackers steal or reuse authentication tokens to maintain access without repeated sign-ins or MFA challenges.
ttps.enhancement: Separated token acquisition from token use: T1528 describes theft, while T1550.001 describes using the application access token represented by the challenge's refresh-token continuation.

mitreAttack.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

pivotSteps.purpose: Find the risky device-code authentication and collect its session ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode" and ResultType == "0"
| where IsRisky and IsInteractive
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the refresh-token activity that contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>" and not(IsInteractive)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IncomingTokenType, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.validationKql:
let Seed = SigninLogs | where AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode" and ResultType == "0" and IsRisky and IsInteractive and isnotempty(SessionId) | project SessionId;
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | where not(IsInteractive) and isnotempty(SessionId) | project SessionId, Flag=AuthenticationDetails | join kind=inner Seed on SessionId | project Flag

ttps.name: OAuth / App Consent Abuse
ttps.description: Attackers grant a service principal broad application permissions, shifting durable access from a compromised user to a non-human identity that can authenticate and act without user interaction.
ttps.enhancement: Narrowed this challenge to app-only permission persistence so it remains distinct from the user-deception and delegated-token behavior in Illicit Consent Grants.

mitreAttack.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

references.title: View activity logs of application permissions
Microsoft Entra security operations for applications

pivotSteps.purpose: Find an app-only Microsoft Graph permission grant and collect its audit correlation and application IDs.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Add app role assignment to service principal"
| where tostring(AdditionalDetails) has_all ("Mail.Read", "Files.Read.All")
| extend OAuthAppId=tostring(TargetResources[0].appId)
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, AuditCorrelationId=tostring(CorrelationId), OAuthAppId

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the audit correlation and application IDs to confirm the permission grant and capture its source IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "OAuthAppPermissionGranted"
| extend AuditCorrelationId=tostring(RawEventData.AuditCorrelationId)
| where AuditCorrelationId == "<AuditCorrelationId>" and OAuthAppId == "<OAuthAppId>"
| project Timestamp, OAuthAppId, IPAddress, ObjectName

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on AppId and IPAddress to the app-only sign-in whose user agent contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where AppId == "<OAuthAppId>" and IPAddress == "<IPAddress>"
| project TimeGenerated, ServicePrincipalName, ResourceDisplayName, UserAgent

ttps.name: Privileged Role Abuse
ttps.description: Attackers assign a powerful Microsoft Entra role to a compromised user and then use the elevated session for background administrative access.
ttps.enhancement: Separated permanent role assignment from PIM activation. This challenge models the former and maps it directly to Additional Cloud Roles rather than implying every privileged action is privilege escalation.

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a Global Administrator assignment and collect the target user and initiating IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Add member to role"
| where tostring(TargetResources) has "Global Administrator"
| extend UserId=tostring(TargetResources[0].id), IPAddress=tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, UserId, IPAddress, TargetResources

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the elevated user and source IP to recover the privileged interactive session ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where UserId == "<UserId>" and IPAddress == "<IPAddress>"
| where AppDisplayName == "Azure Portal"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the elevated background session that contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.name: Service Principal Privilege Escalation
ttps.description: Attackers grant a service principal a privileged directory role or application role, then use the non-human identity to perform sensitive Microsoft Graph operations without MFA.
ttps.enhancement: Focused on a service-principal role assignment rather than conflating role grants with added credentials; the latter is separately mapped to T1098.001 when it occurs.

references.title: Microsoft Entra security operations for applications
View activity logs of application permissions

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a privileged app-role assignment and collect the target service-principal object ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Add app role assignment to service principal"
| where tostring(AdditionalDetails) has "RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory"
| extend ServicePrincipalId=tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, ServicePrincipalId, TargetResources

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on ServicePrincipalId to the app-only sign-in and record its token identifier.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where ServicePrincipalId == "<ServicePrincipalId>"
| project TimeGenerated, ServicePrincipalName, UniqueTokenIdentifier, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UniqueTokenIdentifier to the privileged Graph request whose URI contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where UniqueTokenIdentifier == "<UniqueTokenIdentifier>"
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationId, RequestMethod, RequestUri, ResponseStatusCode

ttps.name: Conditional Access Policy Abuse
ttps.description: Attackers modify Conditional Access policies to weaken MFA, device compliance, or location enforcement while access still appears policy-compliant.
ttps.enhancement: Narrowed the generic Impair Defenses mapping to the dedicated ATT&CK Conditional Access Policies sub-technique and retained the policy-object-to-sign-in proof path.

mitreAttack.name: Modify Authentication Process: Conditional Access Policies

pivotSteps.purpose: Find the Conditional Access policy update and collect its audit correlation ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Update conditional access policy"
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, CorrelationId, TargetResources

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on CorrelationId to recover the changed policy object ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| extend AuditCorrelationId=tostring(RawEventData.AuditCorrelationId)
| where AuditCorrelationId == "<CorrelationId>"
| project Timestamp, ObjectId, AccountId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Expand the evaluated policy list and pivot on ObjectId to the weakened policy; this row contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| mv-expand Policy=ConditionalAccessPolicies
| where tostring(Policy.id) == "<ObjectId>"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, ConditionalAccessStatus, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.name: Directory Reconnaissance
ttps.description: Attackers enumerate cloud users, groups, roles, and privilege relationships to identify high-value accounts and paths for expansion.
ttps.enhancement: Replaced the source slide's AuditLogs List/Get example because directory reads generally are not directory-change audit events. The challenge now correlates Defender for Identity query telemetry to the actor's Entra token and Graph directory requests.

pivotSteps.purpose: Find privileged-account enumeration and collect the actor's Entra object ID and source IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
IdentityQueryEvents
| where QueryType == "EnumerateUsers"
| where Query has "adminCount=1"
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, Query, QueryTarget

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on AccountObjectId and IPAddress to recover the token used by the enumerating identity.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where UserId == "<AccountObjectId>" and IPAddress == "<IPAddress>"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, UniqueTokenIdentifier, AppDisplayName

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UniqueTokenIdentifier to the Graph role-membership query whose URI contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where UniqueTokenIdentifier == "<UniqueTokenIdentifier>"
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationId, RequestMethod, RequestUri, ResponseStatusCode

ttps.name: Session Persistence / Continuous Access
ttps.description: Attackers reuse an established cloud session across services so activity continues without another interactive authentication or MFA prompt.
ttps.enhancement: Clarified that continuous access is an observable timeline pattern rather than a standalone ATT&CK technique; this challenge specifically models application-token reuse under T1550.001.

mitreAttack.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

pivotSteps.purpose: Find the last interactive authentication for a suspicious session and record its session ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0" and IsInteractive
| where AppDisplayName == "Microsoft 365"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to activity in another cloud service without a new interactive sign-in.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| extend SessionId=tostring(SessionData.SessionId)
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>"
| project Timestamp, AccountId, Application, ActionType, SessionId

pivotSteps.purpose: Carry SessionId to the refresh-token continuation whose authentication details contain the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>" and not(IsInteractive)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IncomingTokenType, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.name: Cross-Tenant / B2B Identity Abuse
ttps.description: Attackers retain access through an external guest identity that is added to a sensitive group and authenticates from a different home tenant.
ttps.enhancement: Made cross-tenant status provable through HomeTenantId, ResourceTenantId, and CrossTenantAccessType instead of inferring it from a guest-looking UPN alone.

references.title: Microsoft Entra sign-in log activity details
What are interactive user sign-ins in Microsoft Entra

pivotSteps.purpose: Find an external guest added to a sensitive group and collect the guest object ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Add member to group"
| where tostring(TargetResources) has_all ("Guest", "Incident Response Administrators")
| extend GuestUserId=tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, GuestUserId, TargetResources

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the guest object ID and prove that its home and resource tenants differ.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where UserId == "<GuestUserId>"
| where HomeTenantId != ResourceTenantId and CrossTenantAccessType == "b2bCollaboration"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SessionId, HomeTenantId, ResourceTenantId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the guest's sensitive cloud activity whose raw event evidence contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| extend SessionId=tostring(SessionData.SessionId)
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>" and IsExternalUser
| project Timestamp, AccountId, Application, ActionType, RawEventData

ttps.name: Identity to Infrastructure Access
ttps.description: Attackers use a compromised cloud identity to invoke Azure Run Command, causing code execution inside a virtual machine without an interactive operating-system logon.
ttps.enhancement: Narrowed the broad source concept to Azure Run Command and added the endpoint process proof ATT&CK explicitly recommends for cloud administration commands.

references.title: Run scripts in a Windows VM with Run Command

pivotSteps.purpose: Find the compromised Azure management sign-in and collect the caller identity and source IP.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0" and AppDisplayName == "Azure Portal"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on Caller and CallerIpAddress to the Azure VM Run Command operation and record the ARM resource name.
pivotSteps.kql:
AzureActivity
| where Caller == "<UserPrincipalName>" and CallerIpAddress == "<IPAddress>"
| where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/RUNCOMMAND/ACTION"
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, ResourceName=Resource, CorrelationId, ResourceId

pivotSteps.purpose: Normalize the endpoint FQDN to its first DNS label and pivot on the ARM resource name to the Run Command guest process whose command line contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| extend ResourceName=tostring(split(DeviceName, ".")[0])
| where ResourceName =~ "<ResourceName>"
| where FolderPath has "RunCommandWindows"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

categories.name: Application-Based Adversary Tradecraft
categories.description: How attackers abuse cloud applications, APIs, and automation to access data and persist without interactive users.

ttps.name: API Access Abuse
ttps.description: Attackers abuse application API permissions or service principals to access cloud resources without interactive user sign-ins.
ttps.enhancement: Retained the Graph-focused implementation but distinguishes API execution (T1059.009) from the token material used to authorize it (T1550.001).

mitreAttack.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API
Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

references.title: Microsoft Graph authentication and authorization basics

pivotSteps.purpose: Find the application consent and recover the service principal object ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Consent to application"
| where tostring(AdditionalDetails) has_all ("Files.Read.All", "Directory.Read.All")
| extend ServicePrincipalId=tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, ServicePrincipalId

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on ServicePrincipalId to recover the issued token identifier.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where ServicePrincipalId == "<ServicePrincipalId>"
| project TimeGenerated, AppId, UniqueTokenIdentifier, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UniqueTokenIdentifier to the Graph request that contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where UniqueTokenIdentifier == "<UniqueTokenIdentifier>"
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationId, RequestMethod, RequestUri, ResponseStatusCode

ttps.name: Application Impersonation (On-Behalf-Of Abuse)
ttps.description: Attackers abuse an OAuth On-Behalf-Of flow so a trusted middle-tier application exchanges a user's token and calls downstream APIs with that user's delegated permissions.
ttps.enhancement: Clarified that OBO is a legitimate protocol flow, not an ATT&CK technique by itself. The malicious behavior is use of an acquired application access token under T1550.001.

mitreAttack.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

references.title: Microsoft identity platform OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of flow

pivotSteps.purpose: Find an interactive sign-in whose processing details identify an On-Behalf-Of exchange and record its session ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0"
| where AuthenticationProcessingDetails has "On-Behalf-Of"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the background OBO token exchange and capture the issued token identifier.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>"
| where AuthenticationProtocol == "oAuth2"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, UniqueTokenIdentifier, IncomingTokenType

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UniqueTokenIdentifier to the delegated Graph request whose URI contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where UniqueTokenIdentifier == "<UniqueTokenIdentifier>"
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationId, AccountObjectId, RequestMethod, RequestUri

ttps.name: Cross-Tenant / B2B Application Impersonation
ttps.description: Attackers use an application owned by an external tenant and an accepted trust relationship to call internal APIs as an apparently legitimate partner application.
ttps.enhancement: Made both sides of the boundary explicit with AppOwnerTenantId versus AADTenantId and tied the external app's token to its Graph and cloud-app activity.

mitreAttack.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

pivotSteps.purpose: Find an app-only sign-in whose application owner tenant differs from the resource tenant and collect its token and app IDs.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
| where AppOwnerTenantId != AADTenantId
| project TimeGenerated, AppId, ServicePrincipalName, UniqueTokenIdentifier, IPAddress, AppOwnerTenantId, AADTenantId

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on UniqueTokenIdentifier to the external application's Graph request and record its report ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where UniqueTokenIdentifier == "<UniqueTokenIdentifier>"
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationId, ReportId, IpAddress, RequestUri

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the application and report IDs to the external app's SaaS action whose raw event data contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| where OAuthAppId == "<ApplicationId>" and ReportId == "<ReportId>"
| project Timestamp, Application, AccountId, ActionType, ObjectName, RawEventData

ttps.name: Illicit Consent Grants
ttps.description: Attackers deceive a user into granting delegated OAuth scopes, then redeem the resulting refresh token for background access without another user interaction.
ttps.enhancement: Separated deceptive user consent from app-only administrator permission grants. This challenge follows the user consent through Defender for Cloud Apps to a delegated non-interactive sign-in.

mitreAttack.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

references.title: Microsoft Entra security operations for applications
View activity logs of application permissions

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a user consent granting high-risk delegated scopes and collect the audit correlation ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Consent to application"
| where tostring(AdditionalDetails) has_all ("Principal", "Mail.Read", "offline_access")
| project TimeGenerated, Identity, AuditCorrelationId=tostring(CorrelationId), TargetResources

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the audit correlation ID to recover the consent session ID and OAuth application ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "OAuthAppConsentGranted"
| extend AuditCorrelationId=tostring(RawEventData.AuditCorrelationId), SessionId=tostring(SessionData.SessionId)
| where AuditCorrelationId == "<AuditCorrelationId>"
| project Timestamp, AccountId, OAuthAppId, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the delegated refresh-token sign-in whose authentication details contain the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>" and IncomingTokenType == "refreshToken"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.name: Cloud Resource Enumeration
ttps.description: Attackers issue a burst of Azure Resource Manager list and read operations across compute, storage, and network providers to map reachable infrastructure.
ttps.enhancement: Mapped the behavior to Cloud Infrastructure Discovery and changed the hunt from isolated List/Get strings to a multi-provider burst tied back to the caller's Azure CLI session.

mitreAttack.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API

pivotSteps.purpose: Find a caller rapidly listing resources across at least three Azure resource providers.
pivotSteps.kql:
AzureActivity
| where OperationNameValue contains "/LIST" or OperationNameValue contains "/READ"
| summarize Operations=make_set(OperationNameValue), Providers=dcount(ResourceProviderValue), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by Caller, CallerIpAddress, WindowStart=bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where array_length(Operations) >= 3 and Providers >= 3 and LastSeen - FirstSeen <= 2m

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on Caller and CallerIpAddress to the Azure CLI session used for enumeration.
pivotSteps.kql:
SigninLogs
| where UserPrincipalName == "<Caller>" and IPAddress == "<CallerIpAddress>"
| where AppDisplayName == "Microsoft Azure CLI"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SessionId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on SessionId to the CLI token continuation whose authentication details contain the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where SessionId == "<SessionId>"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IncomingTokenType, AuthenticationDetails

ttps.name: Cloud Data Collection (Non-Mail)
ttps.description: Attackers access SharePoint, OneDrive, or storage data through legitimate APIs or application access without traditional endpoint activity.
ttps.enhancement: Retained and clarified as collection from cloud storage and SharePoint, rather than treating every file API request as generic API abuse.

pivotSteps.purpose: Find suspicious application-based file access and collect the object ID.
pivotSteps.kql:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "FileAccessed" and AccountType == "ServicePrincipal"
| project Timestamp, ObjectId, OAuthAppId, IPAddress

pivotSteps.purpose: Extract the drive-item ID from RequestUri and pivot on ObjectId to confirm API retrieval and its application context.
pivotSteps.kql:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| extend ApiObjectId=extract(@"/drive/items/([^/]+)/content", 1, RequestUri)
| where ApiObjectId == "<ObjectId>"
| project TimeGenerated, ApiObjectId, ReportId, ApplicationId, RequestMethod, RequestUri

pivotSteps.purpose: Pivot on the Graph drive-item ID to the corresponding file-download audit row that contains the flag.
pivotSteps.kql:
OfficeActivity
| where OfficeObjectId == "<ApiObjectId>" and Operation == "FileDownloaded"
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, OfficeObjectId, SourceFileName, ClientIP
